raw_case_text:
A 39-year-old Nigerian woman with history of sickle cell disease presented to our hospital with a chief complaint of increased swelling on her left flank for the past 2 years. She initially noticed the swelling "many years ago" as a 1 cm soft, painless mass. Over the years, the swelling progressively increased to the current size of approximately 10 cm on presentation. She reported no warmth, redness, or drainage of pus or fluid. Six months prior to presentation, the patient began experiencing a dull pain in the midline of her lower back, radiating laterally to the left lower quadrant. It fluctuated in severity but was aggravated with flexion of the back. She reported no recent fevers, fatigue, changes in weight, chills, sweats, hemoptysis, or dyspnea. She did not have any urinary or gastrointestinal symptoms nor did she experience weakness or sensory loss in her lower limbs. The patient immigrated to the United States from Nigeria one year ago. She has no known history of or exposure to TB but did receive the BCG vaccine as a child.
On examination, she was a well appearing young female. Vital signs included BP 118/60 mmHg, HR 66/min, temperature 98.8 F, O2 saturation 97% on room air, and BMI 20.3. She was noted to have icteric sclera and multiple enlarged, nontender, soft, mobile cervical lymph nodes (LNs), the largest being a 2 cm right anterior cervical LN. Inspection of her back revealed a 10 cm x 16 cm well-demarcated fluctuant area without erythema or other skin changes. The area was not tender to palpation, nor were there any areas of focal tenderness at the spine. Range of motion of her back and hips was fully intact. The remainder of the examination including cardiopulmonary, abdominal, and neurologic examination was unremarkable.
Review of her lab tests revealed hemoglobin of 94 g/L, MCV 92.5 fl, RDW 21.7%, reticulocyte count 0.08 of RBCs, leukocyte count 7.4 x 103/muL, and platelet count 317 x 103/muL. Other lab tests included blood urea nitrogen 2.86 mmol/L, serum creatinine 45 mumol/L, AST 65 U/L, ALT 29 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 19 U/L, total bilirubin of 148.8 mumol/L with indirect bilirubin 131.7 mumol/L, LDH 525 U/L, and ESR 28 mm/hr. Rapid HIV testing was negative. Blood cultures drawn at initial evaluation remained sterile after 48 hours.
A computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen and pelvis revealed diskitis/osteomyelitis at the L4-L5 level with adjacent paraspinal and left retroperitoneal abscesses extending to the left lower back/flank subcutaneous tissue and into the epidural space. A follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lumbar spine with and without contrast confirmed these findings of diskitis and osteomyelitis at L4-L5 with an expansile abscess within substance of the disk extending into ventral epidural space with involvement of left L5-S1 and right L4-L5 neural foramina (Figures 1 and 2).
Ultrasound guided drainage of the abscess was attempted but only a small amount of thick tan fluid could be collected as the contents were extremely viscous. Fluid analysis showed glucose <10 mg/dL, protein 5 g/dL, and LDH 4872 U/L. Cell count was unable to be performed due to the fluid's viscosity but differential showed 82% neutrophils. Gram stain and acid-fast staining were negative for any organisms.
Given her history and presentation, a tuberculous cold abscess was high on our differential and the patient was empirically started on the standard anti-TB regimen of isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol. Though she had no neurological symptoms, given the extension of the abscess, both orthopedic and neurosurgery specialists were consulted for surgical drainage of abscess. The patient and neurosurgeons were initially reluctant to perform the procedure and she was therefore discharged on anti-TB medications and pyridoxine.
Upon follow-up at a local TB clinic, she complained of right upper quadrant pain and was found to have elevated transaminases. All of her medications were stopped and a week later she was restarted on rifampin and ethambutol. Four weeks from presentation, cultures from drained abscess revealed Mycobacterium tuberculosis. At this time, the patient was reevaluated by neurosurgery and underwent paraspinal abscess drainage through paravertebral muscles. Following the procedure, she was briefly treated with moxifloxacin as per instructions from the regional TB clinic. At her last clinic visit, six months into her treatment course, she was on isoniazid, rifampin, and pyridoxine without any complaints.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 39-year-old female presented with progressive enlargement of a left flank swelling for 2 years and lower back pain radiating to the left lower quadrant for 6 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 39-year-old female noticed a soft, painless 1 cm mass on her left flank many years ago that progressively increased in size, becoming noticeably larger over the past 2 years to a diameter of 10 cm. Six months prior to presentation, she developed dull lower back pain radiating laterally to the left lower quadrant, fluctuating in intensity and aggravated by spinal flexion. She denied fevers, chills, sweats, weight loss, hemoptysis, dyspnea, gastrointestinal/urinary symptoms, or neurologic deficits.
subjective.past_medical_history: Sickle cell disease. Immigrated to the United States from Nigeria 1 year prior. Childhood BCG vaccination. No known personal history of or exposure to tuberculosis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for dull lower back pain radiating to left lower quadrant, aggravated by spinal flexion. Negative for fevers, chills, night sweats, fatigue, weight changes, hemoptysis, dyspnea, bowel/bladder dysfunction, lower extremity weakness, or numbness. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Well-appearing female. BP 118/60 mmHg, HR 66/min, T 98.8 °F, SpO2 97% on room air, BMI 20.3 kg/m2. Scleral icterus. Multiple enlarged, nontender, soft, mobile cervical lymph nodes (largest 2 cm right anterior cervical). Back: 10 cm x 16 cm well-demarcated, fluctuant mass on left flank without erythema, warmth, drainage, or tenderness; no focal spinal tenderness. Full range of motion of back and hips. Neurological, cardiopulmonary, and abdominal exams unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 94 g/L, MCV 92.5 fL, RDW 21.7%, reticulocyte count 0.08 of RBCs, leukocyte count 7.4 x 103/muL, platelet count 317 x 103/muL. BUN 2.86 mmol/L, serum creatinine 45 mumol/L, AST 65 U/L, ALT 29 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 19 U/L, total bilirubin 148.8 mumol/L (indirect bilirubin 131.7 mumol/L), LDH 525 U/L, ESR 28 mm/hr. Rapid HIV test negative. Blood cultures sterile at 48 hours.
objective.advanced_workup: CT abdomen/pelvis: L4-L5 diskitis and osteomyelitis with paraspinal and left retroperitoneal abscesses extending into left flank subcutaneous tissue and epidural space. MRI lumbar spine: expansile abscess within L4-L5 intervertebral disc extending into ventral epidural space and involving left L5-S1 and right L4-L5 neural foramina. Ultrasound-guided aspiration of abscess yielded viscous tan fluid (glucose <10 mg/dL, protein 5 g/dL, LDH 4872 U/L, 82% neutrophils); Gram stain and acid-fast stain were negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Tuberculous spondylodiscitis (Pott's disease) of L4-L5 with retroperitoneal, epidural, and subcutaneous cold abscess of the left flank, confirmed by fluid cultures from the drained abscess yielding Mycobacterium tuberculosis at 4 weeks. Management & Outcome: Started empirically on 4-drug therapy (isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) plus pyridoxine. Course was complicated by drug-induced transaminitis, necessitating temporary drug cessation and sequential reintroduction with rifampin, ethambutol, and brief moxifloxacin. Following microbiological confirmation, she underwent surgical drainage of the paraspinal abscess via a paravertebral approach. Maintained on isoniazid, rifampin, and pyridoxine at 6-month follow-up with complete symptom resolution and normalization of liver enzymes.
